target: Indonesia punya ribuan pulau, dari Sabang sampai Merauke.
english: Indonesia has thousands of islands, from Sabang to Merauke.
grammar: Dari Sabang sampai Merauke = 'all across Indonesia' — Sabang and Merauke are its far western and eastern ends.

target: Sawah di belakang desa itu hijau sekali setelah musim tanam.
english: The rice fields behind that village are very green after planting season.
grammar: Sawah = a flooded rice field; a dry field is ladang. Pemandangan sawah = rice-field scenery.

target: Kami berjalan kaki melewati sawah menuju air terjun di kaki gunung.
english: We walked past rice fields toward the waterfall at the foot of the mountain.

target: Hutan di pulau ini masih lebat dan penuh suara burung.
english: The forest on this island is still dense and full of bird sounds.

target: Dari puncak gunung, kami bisa melihat laut dan pulau-pulau kecil.
english: From the mountain peak, we can see the sea and the small islands.

target: Air sungai di dekat desa itu jernih dan dingin sekali.
english: The river water near that village is very clear and cold.

target: Nelayan berangkat ke laut sebelum matahari terbit setiap pagi.
english: The fishermen set out to sea before sunrise every morning.
grammar: Matahari terbit = sunrise, matahari terbenam = sunset. Matahari is literally 'eye of the day'.

target: Pasir di pantai sebelah timur pulau ini putih dan halus.
english: The sand on the beach on the east side of this island is white and fine.

target: Ombak di pantai selatan terlalu besar untuk berenang hari ini.
english: The waves at the south beach are too big for swimming today.

target: Petani mulai memanen padi di sawah minggu depan.
english: The farmers start harvesting the rice in the fields next week.
grammar: Rice has three names: padi in the field, beras raw in the bag, nasi cooked on your plate.

target: Kami menginap di desa kecil di kaki gunung berapi.
english: We stayed overnight in a small village at the foot of a volcano.
grammar: Gunung berapi = volcano, literally 'mountain with fire' (api = fire).

target: Danau di atas gunung itu dulunya kawah gunung berapi.
english: The lake on top of that mountain used to be a volcano's crater.

target: Udara di pegunungan jauh lebih sejuk daripada di pantai.
english: The air in the mountains is much cooler than at the beach.
grammar: pe-…-an turns a noun into its whole area: gunung = mountain, pegunungan = mountain range.

target: Banyak monyet liar tinggal di hutan kecil dekat pura itu.
english: Many wild monkeys live in the small forest near that temple.

target: Jalan ke desa itu sempit dan berkelok-kelok di lereng gunung.
english: The road to that village is narrow and winding on the mountainside.

target: Sungai besar itu menjadi jalan utama untuk warga di pedalaman.
english: That big river serves as the main road for people in the interior.

target: Kami menyewa perahu kecil untuk keliling danau sore itu.
english: We rented a small boat to go around the lake that afternoon.

target: Pemandangan matahari terbenam di pantai barat pulau ini terkenal indah.
english: The sunset view on this island's west coast is famously beautiful.

target: Air terjun itu tersembunyi di dalam hutan, satu jam jalan kaki dari desa.
english: That waterfall is hidden inside the forest, an hour's walk from the village.

target: Di musim kemarau, sawah di daerah kami sering kekurangan air.
english: In the dry season, the rice fields in our area often lack water.
grammar: ke-…-an around kurang (less) = to be short of something: kekurangan air = short of water.

target: Anak-anak desa berenang di sungai setiap sore setelah pulang sekolah.
english: The village children swim in the river every afternoon after coming home from school.

target: Kabut turun cepat sekali di gunung, jadi kami turun sebelum gelap.
english: The fog comes down very fast on the mountain, so we went down before dark.

target: Pantai di dekat pelabuhan kotor, lebih baik pergi ke teluk sebelah.
english: The beach near the harbor is dirty; better to go to the next bay over.

target: Orang sini percaya hutan itu harus dijaga karena dianggap keramat.
english: People here believe that forest must be protected because it is considered sacred.
grammar: Keramat = sacred, spiritually charged — said of old trees, graves, and forests people leave undisturbed.

target: Setiap pulau di Indonesia punya bahasa dan makanan khasnya sendiri.
english: Every island in Indonesia has its own distinctive language and food.
grammar: -nya sendiri = its own: makanan khasnya sendiri = its own signature food.

target: Setiap pagi saya berangkat jam enam supaya tidak kena macet.
english: Every morning I leave at six o'clock so I don't get caught in traffic.
grammar: Kena = to get hit by something unpleasant: kena macet = stuck in traffic, kena hujan = caught in the rain.

target: Macet di kota ini sudah biasa, semua orang punya cerita macetnya sendiri.
english: Traffic jams in this city are normal; everyone has their own traffic-jam story.

target: Kalau hujan deras satu jam saja, jalan depan kantor langsung banjir.
english: If it rains hard for just an hour, the street in front of the office floods immediately.

target: Musim hujan berarti musim banjir untuk warga di pinggir sungai.
english: The rainy season means flood season for residents along the river.

target: Polusi udara di kota besar makin parah pada musim kemarau.
english: Air pollution in big cities gets worse and worse in the dry season.
grammar: Makin = increasingly: makin parah = getting worse. Doubled: makin lama makin parah = worse and worse.

target: Banyak orang memakai masker karena polusi udara hari ini buruk sekali.
english: Many people are wearing masks because the air pollution today is really bad.

target: Saya lebih suka naik transportasi umum daripada menyetir sendiri di kota.
english: I prefer taking public transportation to driving myself in the city.
grammar: Umum = public/shared: transportasi umum = public transport, toilet umum = public toilet.

target: Naik kereta ke pusat kota lebih cepat daripada naik mobil.
english: Taking the train downtown is faster than going by car.

target: Bus kota di sini murah, tapi jadwalnya tidak bisa dipercaya.
english: The city buses here are cheap, but their schedule can't be trusted.

target: Kami pindah ke pinggir kota supaya dekat dengan stasiun kereta.
english: We moved to the edge of the city to be close to the train station.

target: Ojek online sangat membantu kalau kamu buru-buru di jam sibuk.
english: App-based motorbike taxis really help when you're in a hurry at rush hour.
grammar: Jam sibuk = rush hour ('busy hours'): berangkat sebelum jam sibuk = leave before rush hour.

target: Trotoar di jalan ini penuh pedagang kaki lima setiap sore.
english: The sidewalk on this street is full of street vendors every afternoon.
grammar: Pedagang kaki lima = street vendor, literally 'five-foot trader', from the five-foot colonial walkway.

target: Suara klakson di jalan besar itu hampir tidak pernah berhenti.
english: The sound of horns on that main road almost never stops.

target: Di jam pulang kantor, kereta ke arah selatan selalu penuh sesak.
english: At the end of the workday, trains heading south are always packed.

target: Kota ini terasa lebih tenang saat libur Lebaran karena banyak warga mudik.
english: This city feels calmer during the Lebaran holiday because many residents go back to their hometowns.

target: Harga rumah di pusat kota terlalu mahal untuk keluarga muda.
english: House prices in the city center are too expensive for young families.

target: Lampu merah di simpang itu lama sekali, bisa sampai tiga menit.
english: The red light at that intersection is really long; it can last up to three minutes.

target: Warga kompleks kami kerja bakti membersihkan selokan setiap bulan.
english: The residents of our housing complex do communal volunteer work cleaning the drains every month.
grammar: Kerja bakti = the neighborhood work day: everyone comes out to clean drains and cut grass together.

target: Selokan yang penuh sampah membuat banjir makin sering terjadi.
english: Drains full of garbage make floods happen more and more often.

target: Kalau banjir datang, warga memindahkan motor mereka ke tempat yang lebih tinggi.
english: When the floods come, residents move their motorbikes to higher ground.

target: Selama musim hujan, banyak keluarga menyimpan barang penting di lantai dua.
english: During the rainy season, many families keep important belongings on the second floor.

target: Setiap tahun ada gedung tinggi baru di pusat kota.
english: Every year there are new tall buildings in the city center.

target: Angkot di kota kecil berhenti di mana saja kalau dipanggil.
english: Minibuses in small towns stop anywhere when hailed.
grammar: Angkot (angkutan kota) = the shared minibus; passengers shout 'Kiri!' (left!) to get dropped off.

target: Suara azan terdengar dari beberapa masjid sekaligus waktu magrib.
english: The call to prayer can be heard from several mosques at once at sunset prayer time.

target: Malam hari, pasar kaget muncul di lapangan dekat rumah kami.
english: At night, a pop-up market appears on the field near our house.
grammar: Pasar kaget = pop-up market, literally 'startled market' — it appears suddenly and is gone by morning.

target: Banyak warga kota besar menghabiskan dua jam sehari di jalan.
english: Many big-city residents spend two hours a day on the road.

target: Pemerintah kota menanam pohon baru di sepanjang jalan utama tahun ini.
english: The city government is planting new trees along the main road this year.

target: Parkir di pusat perbelanjaan itu susah sekali pada akhir pekan.
english: Parking at that shopping mall is really difficult on weekends.

target: Taman kota baru itu ramai keluarga setiap Minggu pagi.
english: That new city park is crowded with families every Sunday morning.

target: Meskipun macet dan gerah, saya tetap sayang kota ini.
english: Even though it's jammed with traffic and muggy, I still love this city.

target: Tolong buang sampah pada tempatnya, jangan ke selokan.
english: Please throw trash where it belongs, not into the drain.
grammar: Buang sampah pada tempatnya ('bin your trash') is the sign painted on walls all over Indonesia.

target: Sampah plastik dari kota sering berakhir di laut dan pantai.
english: Plastic waste from the city often ends up in the sea and on beaches.

target: Kami membawa tas belanja sendiri supaya tidak memakai kantong plastik.
english: We bring our own shopping bags so we don't use plastic bags.

target: Di sekolah, anak-anak belajar memisahkan sampah basah dan sampah kering.
english: At school, the children learn to separate wet trash and dry trash.
grammar: Trash sorts by wetness: sampah basah = wet (food) waste, sampah kering = dry (paper, plastic) waste.

target: Botol dan kaleng bekas ini bisa didaur ulang jadi barang baru.
english: These used bottles and cans can be recycled into new things.
grammar: Daur ulang = recycle ('re-cycle'): bisa didaur ulang = can be recycled.

target: Bapak itu memungut botol plastik di pantai setiap pagi.
english: That man collects plastic bottles on the beach every morning.

target: Sedotan plastik sekarang diganti sedotan kertas di banyak kafe.
english: Plastic straws are now replaced with paper straws in many cafes.

target: Jangan bakar sampah di halaman, asapnya mengganggu tetangga.
english: Don't burn trash in the yard; the smoke bothers the neighbors.

target: Truk sampah lewat di kompleks kami setiap Selasa dan Jumat pagi.
english: The garbage truck comes through our complex every Tuesday and Friday morning.

target: Air bersih makin susah didapat di beberapa daerah saat kemarau panjang.
english: Clean water is getting harder to find in some areas during a long dry season.

target: Kami menampung air hujan untuk menyiram tanaman di halaman.
english: We collect rainwater to water the plants in the yard.

target: Matikan lampu dan AC kalau ruangan tidak dipakai, hemat listrik.
english: Turn off the lights and the AC when the room isn't in use — save electricity.
grammar: Hemat = economical, to save on: hemat listrik = save electricity, hemat air = save water.

target: Sungai di tengah kota itu mulai bersih lagi setelah warga berhenti membuang sampah.
english: The river in the middle of the city is getting clean again after residents stopped dumping garbage.

target: Pabrik di hulu sungai itu didenda karena mencemari air.
english: The factory upstream on that river was fined for polluting the water.
grammar: Hulu = upstream, hilir = downstream: pabrik di hulu = a factory upstream.

target: Banyak hewan laut mati karena menelan sampah plastik.
english: Many sea animals die from swallowing plastic waste.

target: Kampung ini terkenal karena warganya rajin mendaur ulang sampah.
english: This neighborhood is famous because its residents diligently recycle their trash.

target: Penebangan hutan di gunung membuat banjir makin parah di daerah hilir.
english: Logging the forests in the mountains makes floods worse and worse in the downstream areas.

target: Pemandu wisata meminta kami tidak meninggalkan sampah apa pun di gunung.
english: The tour guide asked us not to leave any trash at all on the mountain.

target: Udara segar dan air jernih sekarang terasa makin mahal di kota besar.
english: Fresh air and clear water now feel more and more costly in big cities.

target: Lingkungan yang bersih dimulai dari kebiasaan kecil di rumah sendiri.
english: A clean environment starts with small habits in your own home.

target: Nyamuk di kamar ini banyak sekali, saya tidak bisa tidur semalaman.
english: There are so many mosquitoes in this room, I couldn't sleep all night.
grammar: Nyamuk (mosquito) complaints are national small talk: Nyamuknya banyak, ya! = so many mosquitoes, huh!

target: Jangan lupa pakai obat nyamuk sebelum tidur, ya.
english: Don't forget to put on mosquito repellent before bed, okay?
grammar: Obat covers any remedy: obat nyamuk = mosquito repellent, literally 'mosquito medicine'.

target: Saya digigit nyamuk sepuluh kali waktu duduk di teras tadi malam.
english: I got bitten by mosquitoes ten times while sitting on the porch last night.

target: Kucing kampung itu setiap pagi menunggu di depan warung ikan.
english: That street cat waits in front of the fish stall every morning.
grammar: Kampung after an animal = local/free-range: kucing kampung = street cat, ayam kampung = village chicken.

target: Ayam tetangga berkokok jam empat pagi, lebih pagi daripada alarm saya.
english: The neighbor's rooster crows at four in the morning, earlier than my alarm.

target: Ayam kampung nenek berjalan bebas di halaman sepanjang hari.
english: Grandma's free-range chickens walk around the yard freely all day.

target: Cicak di dinding itu makan nyamuk, jadi jangan diusir.
english: The geckos on the wall eat mosquitoes, so don't chase them away.
grammar: Cicak = the little house gecko on every Indonesian wall — a welcome guest, it eats mosquitoes.

target: Suara cicak kadang membuat tamu asing kaget pada malam hari.
english: The sound of the geckos sometimes startles foreign guests at night.

target: Kami memelihara dua ekor kucing dan beberapa ekor ayam.
english: We keep two cats and several chickens.
grammar: Ekor (tail) counts animals: dua ekor kucing = two cats, seekor ayam = one chicken.

target: Anjing tetangga menggonggong setiap kali tukang pos datang.
english: The neighbor's dog barks every time the mail carrier comes.

target: Ikan di kolam belakang rumah paman besar-besar sekali.
english: The fish in the pond behind my uncle's house are all really big.
grammar: Doubling an adjective for a plural subject = all of them: besar-besar = all big.

target: Burung-burung kecil ribut sekali di pohon mangga setiap pagi.
english: The little birds are very noisy in the mango tree every morning.

target: Kambing milik pak RT makan rumput di lapangan kompleks.
english: The goats belonging to the neighborhood head graze on the field in the complex.
grammar: Pak RT = head of the smallest neighborhood unit (Rukun Tetangga) — the person everyone knows.

target: Sapi-sapi itu menyeberang jalan pelan-pelan, semua mobil menunggu.
english: The cows cross the road slowly; all the cars wait.

target: Monyet di dekat candi suka mengambil kacamata dan topi turis.
english: The monkeys near the temple like to take tourists' glasses and hats.

target: Hati-hati, monyet di sana berani merebut makanan dari tangan kamu.
english: Be careful — the monkeys there are bold enough to snatch food right out of your hand.

target: Suara katak terdengar keras dari sawah waktu musim hujan.
english: The sound of frogs can be heard loudly from the rice fields in the rainy season.

target: Semut langsung datang kalau ada makanan manis di meja.
english: Ants come right away if there's sweet food on the table.

target: Tikus di plafon berisik sekali, tapi kucing kami hanya tidur.
english: The mice in the ceiling are really noisy, but our cat just sleeps.

target: Kupu-kupu warna-warni datang ke bunga di halaman setiap pagi.
english: Colorful butterflies come to the flowers in the yard every morning.

target: Bapak itu menjual burung dan sangkarnya di pasar hewan.
english: That man sells birds and their cages at the animal market.

target: Anak saya takut kecoak, padahal dia berani memegang ular kecil.
english: My child is afraid of cockroaches, yet dares to hold a small snake.
grammar: Padahal = even though / when in fact — it flags a surprising contrast between two facts.

target: Ular sawah kadang masuk ke halaman rumah waktu musim panen.
english: Rice-field snakes sometimes come into the yard during harvest season.

target: Di pasar burung, suara ratusan burung terdengar dari jauh.
english: At the bird market, the sound of hundreds of birds can be heard from far away.

target: Nyamuk demam berdarah biasanya menggigit pada pagi dan sore hari.
english: Dengue mosquitoes usually bite in the morning and late afternoon.
grammar: Demam berdarah (DBD) = dengue fever, literally 'bleeding fever' — a rainy-season worry.

target: Hari ini gerah sekali, baju saya basah padahal hanya duduk saja.
english: It's really muggy today; my shirt is soaked even though I'm just sitting.
grammar: Gerah = muggy, hot-and-sticky (how you feel); panas = hot in general: hari ini gerah = it's sticky today.

target: Kalau gerah begini, biasanya sebentar lagi hujan deras turun.
english: When it's this muggy, usually heavy rain comes down before long.

target: Sudah seminggu mendung terus, jemuran tidak pernah kering.
english: It's been overcast nonstop for a week; the laundry never dries.
grammar: Terus after a verb or adjective = keeps on: mendung terus = overcast nonstop, hujan terus = keeps raining.

target: Langit mendung terus dari pagi, tapi hujannya tidak turun-turun.
english: The sky has been overcast since morning, but the rain just won't fall.
grammar: Doubling after tidak = just won't: tidak turun-turun = (the rain) never actually falls.

target: Sekarang musim pancaroba, pagi panas sekali, sore hujan angin.
english: It's the transition season now — mornings are very hot, afternoons bring wind and rain.
grammar: Musim pancaroba = the unstable switch between wet and dry seasons: sunny mornings, stormy afternoons.

target: Banyak orang kena flu pada musim pancaroba seperti ini.
english: Lots of people catch the flu in a transition season like this.

target: Angin kencang semalam menumbangkan pohon besar di ujung jalan.
english: Last night's strong wind knocked down the big tree at the end of the street.

target: Petir keras sekali tadi, sampai anak-anak lari masuk rumah.
english: The thunder was really loud just now — the kids even ran into the house.

target: Cabut kabel televisi kalau ada petir, itu kebiasaan ibu saya.
english: Unplug the TV cable when there's lightning — that's my mother's habit.

target: Gerimis begini biasanya berhenti sendiri sebelum sore.
english: Drizzle like this usually stops on its own before late afternoon.

target: Hujan angin kemarin membuat listrik mati tiga jam di daerah kami.
english: Yesterday's rainstorm knocked the power out for three hours in our area.
grammar: Mati works for power and machines: listrik mati = the power is out, lampunya mati = the light is off.

target: Setelah hujan semalaman, udara pagi ini segar dan sejuk sekali.
english: After it rained all night, the air this morning is really fresh and cool.

target: Awan gelap datang dari arah laut, nelayan cepat-cepat pulang.
english: Dark clouds are coming from the direction of the sea; the fishermen hurry home.

target: Debu jalanan makin tebal pada akhir musim kemarau seperti sekarang.
english: The road dust gets thicker and thicker at the end of the dry season, like now.

target: Ramalan cuaca bilang minggu ini hujan setiap sore.
english: The weather forecast says it will rain every afternoon this week.

target: Jangan percaya langit cerah di musim pancaroba, bawa payung terus.
english: Don't trust a clear sky in the transition season — always carry an umbrella.

target: Banjir besar biasanya datang waktu hujan deras bertemu air laut pasang.
english: Big floods usually come when heavy rain meets a high tide.
grammar: Pasang = high tide: air laut pasang = the tide is in. The opposite is surut = the tide is out.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini datang terlambat, para petani mulai khawatir.
english: The rainy season came late this year; the farmers are starting to worry.

target: Sore-sore begini enaknya minum teh hangat sambil melihat hujan.
english: On a late afternoon like this, the nice thing to do is drink warm tea while watching the rain.
grammar: Enaknya + verb = the nice thing to do is: enaknya minum teh = it'd be lovely to have tea.

target: Baju yang dijemur dari pagi belum kering juga karena mendung.
english: The clothes that have been hung out since morning still aren't dry because it's overcast.
grammar: Juga after belum = STILL not: belum kering juga = still not dry (and it's getting annoying).

target: Kata orang tua, kalau semut pindah rumah, hujan besar akan datang.
english: According to the elders, when ants move house, a big rain is coming.

target: Suhu di kota pantai jarang turun di bawah dua puluh lima derajat.
english: The temperature in coastal cities rarely drops below twenty-five degrees.

target: Kalau kemarau panjang, warga desa antre air bersih dari truk tangki.
english: In a long dry season, villagers line up for clean water from tanker trucks.

target: Hujan pertama setelah kemarau panjang membuat jalanan bau tanah.
english: The first rain after a long dry season makes the streets smell of earth.
grammar: Bau + noun = smells of: bau tanah = smells of earth, bau asap = smells of smoke.

target: Cuaca boleh gerah, tapi es kelapa muda selalu jadi penyelamat.
english: The weather may be muggy, but young coconut ice is always the savior.
grammar: Boleh here = 'may well be': cuaca boleh gerah, tapi... = the weather may be muggy, but...
